existing_localTerm:
Constitution's category is ethnic groups, whose stated right covers fine customs and cultures
Education Law's wording for these learners is of ethnic origin, a support category
existing_standing:
Constitution Art. 110 makes Lao the language and script officially used
Ethnic groups' constitutional right runs to fine customs and cultures, not to language
Constitutional education duty to ethnic groups is framed as access, alongside remote areas
A 2004 review counts 82 officially recognised languages in the country
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
Education Law Art. 44 makes Lao the official language for teaching and learning
UNESCO PEER: the official national language remains the medium of instruction in public schools

existing_taughtAsSubject:
Statute's subject-language article covers foreign languages, English compulsory from grade three
2004 review found curriculum and textbooks focused on mainstream culture and language

existing_localTerm:
Statute's category is citizens 'whose native language is not Georgian'
Abkhazian is the only such language the law names, and only for Abkhazia
Law also makes Georgian Sign Language a language of instruction
existing_standing:
Non-Georgian-medium schools timetable Georgian as a second language
They also timetable the ethnic minority language as a subject in its own right
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
Law on General Education 2005 Art 4(1): medium is Georgian, in Abkhazia Georgian or Abkhazian
Whole-school provision: the vehicle is a non-Georgian-medium school, not a lesson-level right
Art 4(3): citizens whose native language is not Georgian may be schooled fully in it
Right runs "in accordance with the National Curriculum, as provided for by the legislation"
Since 2010 Azeri and Armenian entrants reach higher education via quota plus a Georgian year
existing_taughtAsSubject:
The mandatory subject runs the other way: Georgian must be taught in minority-medium schools
Art 4(3): teaching of the official language is mandatory in such institutions
In Abkhazia, whichever official language is the medium, the other must also be taught
Teach Georgian as a Second Language programme targets minority-populated regions

existing_localTerm:
Decree No 13 of 2026 calls Kurdish a lugha wataniyya, a national language
The decree speaks of Syrian Kurdish citizens and their cultural and linguistic identity
The term is fixed by presidential decree and the education ministry's executive instructions
existing_standing:
Arabic is the official language of the country under the 2025 Constitutional Declaration
Article 3 of Decree 13 of 2026 treats Kurdish as a national language
It reaches state and private schools where Kurds are a notable share of the population
The decree requires the state to protect cultural and linguistic diversity
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
Pupils may take social studies, history, geography and philosophy in Kurdish or Arabic
That option is limited to the first academic year after the decision takes effect
existing_taughtAsSubject:
Kurdish is taught at all educational levels and forms part of the approved curricula
An amending decision of 27 August 2026 sets three classes a week beside Arabic and English
January 2026 executive instructions made it optional at two periods a week in all grades
The decree allows it within optional curricula or as a cultural and educational activity

existing_localTerm:
Constitution's own phrase is 'current languages in the country', not minority
Six of them can become a third official language where locally in the majority
State is bound to 'foster and develop all languages of Afghanistan'
existing_standing:
Constitution art. 43: state to provide teaching of native languages where they are spoken
In practice they are taught as subjects only, never as a medium
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
2008 Education Law Art 32: public institutions teach in one of the state official languages
Medium is Pashto or Dari, chosen by the majority language of the area (UNESCO PEER)
Constitution 2004 Art 43: state to prepare the ground for teaching mother tongues where spoken
Both sources describe the pre-August 2021 framework; the position since was not established
existing_taughtAsSubject:
School books produced in Baluchi, Nuristani, Pamiri, Pashaee, Turkmeni and Uzbeki
2008 Education Law makes learning Pashto and Dari compulsory in schools
2014 Inclusive and Child Friendly Education Policy names language minorities as at risk
This is the framework as it stood before August 2021

existing_localTerm:
The constitutional category is the national language, and it names Dhivehi
The curriculum calls Dhivehi the students' first language
existing_standing:
Dhivehi is the national language of the Maldives under the 2008 Constitution
The Education Act makes respect for the Dhivehi language an object of the system
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
Dhivehi is the recommended language of instruction in the foundation years
From Primary onwards the medium is English, or Arabic in specialist schools
Set by curriculum recommendation, with schools told to adopt English medium gradually
Full immersion that discourages mother tongue use within school is discouraged
existing_taughtAsSubject:
Dhivehi shall be taught at every school, by statute
Required at preschool, primary, secondary and higher secondary alike
The curriculum places Dhivehi in the Language and Communication area beside English

existing_localTerm:
Constitution's term is nations and nationalities living on the territory of the republic
UNESCO PEER profile calls the same populations national groups and ethnic groups
existing_standing:
Tajik is the state language under Article 2 of the Constitution
All nations and nationalities hold a constitutional right to use their native language
Courts sit in the state language or the language of the area's majority population
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
State language is the main medium in educational institutions under the Law on Education
Citizens may choose their language of instruction alongside study of the state language
Schools in areas of high ethnic concentration may use those groups' native languages
620 of 3,836 general schools teach in Tajik and Uzbek, 224 in Uzbek, 36 in Kyrgyz

existing_localTerm:
The constitution's phrase is regional and tribal languages, set against Persian
Article 19 speaks of ethnic group or tribe, and bars privilege from race or language
The terms are fixed in the 1979 constitution as amended through 1989
existing_standing:
Persian is the official language and script of Iran and the lingua franca of its people
Regional and tribal languages are allowed in addition to Persian, not made official
The allowance sits in Chapter II on the official language of the country
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
Official documents, correspondence, texts and textbooks must be in Persian language and script
In schools the permitted use is teaching their literature, not instruction through them
existing_taughtAsSubject:
Teaching the literature of regional and tribal languages in schools is allowed, not required
The permission reaches their literature rather than the languages themselves
Arabic by contrast must be taught in all classes of secondary school and all areas of study

existing_localTerm:
Jeju's word is Jejueo, the Jeju language, carried in a provincial ordinance since 2007
Defined as the traditional speech of Jeju residents, tied to islanders' cultural identity
National law calls it jiyeogeo, regional speech, kept inside Korean rather than beside it
existing_standing:
State and local governments must work to preserve regional speech under the Framework Act
Jeju's instrument is a provincial ordinance made under article 4 of that Framework Act
A Jeju language committee reviews the basic plan and the orthographic norm
existing_mediumOfInstruction: Not established from the sources consulted. Article 13 of the Jeju Language Preservation and Promotion Ordinance provides for school education for the language's preservation and dissemination, has the Superintendent support related activities at schools of every level, and lets the governor fund that teaching within the budget, but sets no medium of instruction; the Framework Act on the Korean Language is the instrument above it and names Korean.
existing_taughtAsSubject:
The governor may settle school-education matters with the provincial education superintendent
The superintendent must make and run policies to activate Jeju language school education
Funding for Jeju language teaching in schools is discretionary and within budget
Courses and textbooks are developed for anyone wanting to learn the language

Law of Turkmenistan on Education, 5 June 2021 (as amended 2023), art. 5, CIS Legislation consolidator translation

existing_localTerm:
Constitution's term is native language, guaranteed to every citizen
Education Law uses the same phrase, native language, in its languages article
existing_standing:
Turkmen is the state language, and every citizen is guaranteed use of their native language
The state assists citizens in studying the native language, under other legislation
Judicial proceedings run in the state language, with an interpreter for others
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
Turkmen is the main language of training in institutions of all types
All educational institutions must provide training in the state language
A foreign language may be the main language of training in some institutions
existing_taughtAsSubject: Not established from the sources consulted. The Education Law's article on languages of training and education makes foreign languages obligatory subjects in general and professional programmes, but provides for the native language only as state assistance to citizens studying it under other legislation, and names no such language as a school subject.
